text.p: The privatisation agency on Wednesday approved the privatisation plan of Estonia's largest alcohol producer Liviko, which will be proposed to the government.
"The privatisation will be carried out in two phases," Jaak Leimann, the minister of economics, told a news conference.
The agency plans to sell 44 percent of its shares in a public offering in the second half of the year, Leimann said.
Some 30 percent of Liviko's shares will be sold via a tender after preliminary negotiations. A final 21 percent of shares will be sold in a public offering.
"Hopefully it will all happen next year," Leimann added.
Five percent of Liviko's shares have already been sold to the public and are traded on the OTC market.
